This matches all the observed features. Exact numbers (0.03, 0.003, 0.0268, 0.19) not checked against the full text, which was read only via a machine review page; the couplings J2=0.28, J3=0.14 were inferred by the first pass, not confirmed. Pattern looks genuine, not an artifact.

full_text:
I'm overturning the first pass in one respect: this is **KNOWN**, not KNOWN-VARIANT. The behaviour is the main result of a recent preprint whose simulation setup matches yours almost exactly. The first pass found the right paper but called it a variant only because it couldn't read the paper in full.

**The matching paper.** It is arXiv:2609.15941, "Fractional vortices in a spin-isotropic spiral spin liquid", by Glittum, Yan and Reuther, submitted 14 September 2026. I could read only a machine-written review page (Pith) and the paper's Zenodo dataset entry, not the paper itself. According to the review:
- **Same setup.** The paper runs Monte Carlo simulations on a 200×200 lattice with J₁-J₂-J₃ interactions (δ=0.03) that detect these vortices via the G_μν tensor, measure their densities, and observe binding below an order-by-disorder transition.
- **Same commonest defect.** The basic defects are half-vortices, each carrying a π winding of the spiral wave vector together with a π rotation of the spin frame. A π winding is half a turn, which matches your wave-vector winding of 0.5.
- **Same order-parameter space.** It is [U(1)×SO(3)]/ℤ₂, where reversing the spiral wave vector is equivalent to reversing the spiral-plane normal. Your rarer "spin-frame-only" defects (0.003 per site) fit the classification: For odd u the defects are fractional half-vortices (v = ±i), while even u gives conventional or ℤ₂ vortices.
- **Same temperature behaviour.** The simulations show these vortices are dense in the spiral-spin-liquid regime, and bind tightly below an order-by-disorder phase transition, eventually fusing to vacuum. That matches your dense defects at intermediate temperature (0.03 per site) and the sharp transition at T ≈ 0.027.

**Earlier work behind it.**
- Yan & Reuther, PRR 4, 023175 (2022), studied the XY-spin version. They showed that the local momentum vector field can carry topological defects in the form of vortices, with snapshots from Monte Carlo simulations of a 400×400 square lattice XY model with δ = 0.03. That version has only integer vortices.
- The broad specific-heat hump followed by an order-by-disorder transition is standard spiral-spin-liquid behaviour (Bergman et al., Nature Physics 2007). In that work a broad spiral spin-liquid regime emerges at higher temperatures, and entropy-driven order sets in at lower temperature.

**What I couldn't verify.** Your exact numbers (0.03, 0.003, 0.0268, 0.19) and the couplings J2 = 0.28, J3 = 0.14 are still unchecked against the paper. Those couplings were inferred by the first pass from δ = 0.03 and J3 = J2/2, not read from the paper. The quantities and orders of magnitude match qualitatively, and differences in numbers alone would not make this new.

**Genuine or artifact?** It looks genuine. The two specific-heat features at different temperatures, the strong imbalance between half-vortices and spin-frame-only defects, and the half-turn winding are all consistent with what the theory predicts. None of it suggests random colouring, an inert field, numerical divergence or a frozen state.
